source.title: Open Problems and Conjectures: On third-order rational difference equations, part 1

trace.notes: Normalized the input as a zbMATH bibliographic resolver URL with trailing identifier 5261905.

Failure modes: blocked_or_challenged for the zbMATH web interface and paywalled_or_restricted or metadata_only for the publisher DOI landing and full-text pages. A local shell fetch of https://zbmath.org/5261905 returned a Cloudflare challenge rather than readable source text. Local resolver metadata in outputs/shards/open-problems-shard-1.csv linked zbMATH identifier 5261905 to DOI 10.1080/10236190701871877, but that metadata does not contain the technical problem statements.

Publisher-indexed metadata for DOI 10.1080/10236190701871877 identified the exact work as Open Problems and Conjectures with subtitle On third-order rational difference equations, part 1, by E. Camouzis and G. Ladas, Journal of Difference Equations and Applications 14(3), pages 333-343, 2008. This metadata was used only for source identity, title recovery, and bounded recovery, not for question extraction.

Ran exact-work recovery attempts using the zbMATH identifier 5261905, DOI 10.1080/10236190701871877, the exact title On third-order rational difference equations, part 1, and the authors Camouzis and Ladas. The Taylor & Francis DOI landing and full-text pages exposed metadata and access controls rather than readable full text. ResearchGate candidates found during recovery corresponded to different works, including the 2008 part 2 article with DOI 10.1080/10236190801912308 and the 2006 article When does local asymptotic stability imply global attractivity in rational equations. Book candidates for Dynamics of Third-Order Rational Difference Equations with Open Problems and Conjectures were rejected because they are not the same DOI article source. No readable exact-work PDF or full HTML source was recovered within the bounded pass.

No candidates were mapped, extracted, rewritten, deduplicated, or accepted because no readable PDF or HTML full-text artifact could be confirmed and accessed as the same exact zbMATH source. The workflow forbids extracting questions from resolver metadata, abstracts, citation pages, search snippets, paywalled pages, or different works.
Saved final JSON to outputs/parse-paper/5261905.json and outputs/latest.json.
